## Type of change

- [ ] New recipe
- [ ] Update to an existing recipe
- [ ] Fix — typo, broken link, stale instructions
- [ ] Repo housekeeping

## If you're adding or changing a recipe

The bar is the **Contributing** section of the README. Check what applies:

- [ ] **Prerequisites stated** — which connectors, which account tier.
- [ ] **Preferences are placeholders.** Anything a reader might reasonably choose differently is marked `«LIKE_THIS»`, not hardcoded to your setup.
- [ ] **Tradeoffs explained**, not just listed. "A is faster, B catches more" beats "pick A or B."
- [ ] **Limitations named.** If a tool can't do something a reader would expect it to, say so before they find out the hard way.
- [ ] **Self-contained.** The prompt block works pasted into a fresh session with no prior context.
- [ ] **You ran it live at least once** and the recipe reflects what actually happened, not what you expect would happen.
- [ ] **No personal data anywhere** — no names, emails, locations, account or playlist or task IDs, no share links. Recipes get written by copying a working setup, which is exactly how these leak. Re-read your prompt block and examples with fresh eyes.
- [ ] **Listed in the Recipes table** in `README.md`.
